entity_kinds.definition: A legally constituted entity identified under an applicable registry or authoritative legal record.
An organized body whose legal status may be unresolved or out of scope.
A market-facing name or identity that may be operated by one or more legal entities.
An offered product or service with its own lifecycle and provider relationship.
A coordinated body of work or maintained open-source project, not automatically a legal entity or product.
A foundation or stewarding organization, distinct from projects it hosts.
An authority that publishes standards or specifications within a declared scope.
A multi-party association or collaboration that may lack a single operating legal identity.
A public-sector authority or agency established by law or government action.
An institution whose relevant role is research or scholarship.
A membership, accreditation or professional governance organization.
A versioned software or data artifact distinct from its project, product and operator.

relationship_kinds.definition: An entity operates a product, service or brand during a declared valid-time interval.
An entity maintains a project or artifact without necessarily owning its semantics.
An entity has a declared stewardship role for a project, standard or vocabulary.
A product is offered by a provider entity under a bounded evidence claim.
A project is hosted or governed by an organization or foundation.
A legal entity is a subsidiary of another under an identified authority and valid time.
A legal entity is the direct accounting-consolidating parent under the applicable reporting scope.
A legal entity is the ultimate accounting-consolidating parent under the applicable reporting scope.
A bounded acquisition event relates predecessor and acquiring entities without implying product or semantic identity.
An entity ceased or changed through a documented merger into another entity.
The same entity adopted a documented successor name at a valid time.
An entity, product, project or artifact precedes another without asserting identity.
An entity, product, project or artifact succeeds another without asserting identity.
A versioned resource is a modified or updated edition of another resource.
A versioned resource is an instance of an unversioned or concept-level resource.
An authoritative identifier maps to the same entity within the identifier authority's scope.

resolution_laws: No relation is inferred from a normalized name match.
Every temporal or ownership relation requires a claim-bound evidence locator.
Legal-entity parentage does not imply product ownership, semantic authority or implementation responsibility.
Version and succession relations preserve kind and scope instead of collapsing all predecessors into one identity.
